arguments.value: 31-year-old woman with a one-month history of severe headache and neck pain, followed by recent gait instability, vertigo, right arm weakness, and cerebellar signs. MRI showed a 51 × 48 mm right cerebellar mass causing mass effect, obstructive hydrocephalus, and tonsillar wedging. She underwent right suboccipital craniectomy with radical tumor resection; pathology confirmed small-cell glioblastoma of the posterior fossa. She then received radiotherapy plus temozolomide chemotherapy and remained clinically stable without recurrence on follow-up for over two years.
